message.content:
Here’s a mix of classic, cult‑favorite, and contemporary horror films that have earned a reputation for being genuinely scary:

| # | Title | Year | Director | Why It’s Worth Watching |
|---|-------|------|----------|------------------------|
| 1 | **The Exorcist** | 1973 | William Friedkin | A landmark in supernatural terror; its unsettling atmosphere still feels fresh. |
| 2 | **Halloween** | 1978 | John Carpenter | The original slasher that introduced Michael Myers and set the template for the genre. |
| 3 | **The Shining** | 1980 | Stanley Kubrick | A psychological nightmare based on Stephen King’s novel, with iconic imagery and haunting score. |
| 4 | **A Nightmare on Elm Street** | 1984 | Wes Craven | Freddy Krueger’s dream‑based killings made this a defining teen‑slasher. |
| 5 | **The Silence of the Lambs** | 1991 | Jonathan Demme | A chilling crime thriller featuring Hannibal Lecter and Clarice Starling. |
| 6 | **Scream** | 1996 | Wes Craven | A meta‑slasher that revitalized the genre with self‑aware humor and sharp twists. |
| 7 | **The Ring** | 2002 | Gore Verbinski | An American remake of a Japanese film that brought a creepy viral‑tale vibe to Hollywood. |
| 8 | **28 Days Later** | 2002 | Danny Boyle | A post‑apocalyptic zombie film that emphasized speed and emotional stakes over gore. |
| 9 | **Paranormal Activity** | 2007 | Oren Peli | Low‑budget found‑footage horror that created a new wave of realistic scares. |
|10 | **Hereditary** | 2018 | Ari Aster | A disturbing family drama that escalates into supernatural dread with a masterful build‑up. |
|11 | **Get Out** | 2017 | Jordan Peele | A socially conscious horror that blends satire with genuine terror. |
|12 | **Midsommar** | 2019 | Ari Aster | A daylight horror that turns a pastoral festival into a nightmarish ritual. |
|13 | **It Follows** | 2014 | David Robert Mitchell | A unique premise where a curse is transmitted through sexual contact, creating constant tension. |
|14 | **The Babadook** | 2014 | Jennifer Kent | A psychological horror that uses a monster as a metaphor for grief and mental illness. |
|15 | **Us** | 2019 | Jordan Peele | A psychological thriller that flips the “other” trope onto a family’s own doppelgängers. |

Feel free to pick any of these depending on whether you want supernatural chills, psychological dread, or slasher thrills!
